newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada court rules Saudi dissident a "terrorist".
newsitem.headline: Canada court rules Saudi dissident a "terrorist".

text.p: Canada's federal court ruled on Monday that a man suspected of being a driver involved in the massive truck bomb in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. airmen last year is a terrorist.
Federal court Judge Donna McGillis ruled that a government certificate declaring Saudi dissident Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh a terrorist was reasonable.
"I have no hesitation whatsoever (of declaring the certificate reasonable)," McGillis said as she made her ruling.
Sayegh's lawyer waived his client's opportunity to defend himself publicly in court.
"His testimany in this matter was crucial," McGillis said in her ruling.

The Canadian government has alleged that Sayegh conducted surveillance at the site of last year's bombing of the Khobar Towers, a complex housing U.S. military personnel outside the Saudi city of Dhahran. The bombing killed 19 U.S. airmen and injured 400 people.
Sayegh, 28, will now proceed through immigration hearings, and is expected to be ordered out of the country. He was arrested in Ottawa in March.
